sentence: This project studies how cells move and how that movement shapes tissue, using live microscopy, genetics and computational sciences.
This project studies how a protein controls the way pancreatic cancer cells scavenge nutrients to survive and progress.
This project studies calcium permeable ion channels and their synaptic function, and how hearing loss affects them.
This project tries to find out how host non-coding RNAs help Orientia survive and cause disease during infection.
This project studies how an epigenetic regulator changes the tumor microenvironment and helps pancreatic cancer progress.
This project takes part in a national clinical trials network that develops treatments for cancer patients.
This project builds a fluorescence-based technique to study how proteins move inside photoreceptor cells.
This project studies how RNA modifications in microglia change gene expression and contribute to Alzheimer’s Disease.
This project studies how changes in the dopamine system drive depression symptoms in a model of chronic neuropathic pain.
This project maps molecules linked to metabolism in kidney tissue to find the pathways that matter in kidney disease.
This project studies how different regions of the alveoli in the lung respond to inhaled agents, using a real-time imaging platform.
This project studies how genetic elements in bacteria work and how they can be programed as CRISPR-Cas tools for gene editing.
This project builds a therapy that reprograms B cells to secrete antibodies against HIV.
This project tries to find out how skin bacteria cause T cell responses without inflammation.
This project studies how a peptide called endotrophin may signal to promote atherosclerosis in mice.
This project tests whether an image contrast agent can find the cause of obstruction in the bile ducts, using a flexible fiber instrument.
This project explores methods to make pH dependent antibodies that target certain microenvironments.
This project studies how a common mutation in Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor stimulates an anti-tumor immune response through T cells.
This project works on improving genetic testing for hereditary cancer syndromes.
This project studies how pediatric metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease develops and how it differs from adult disease.
